executive_summary.headline: Claude Duet puts a proactive personal agent in the same race as Dots, Muse and Grok Bot.
executive_summary.body: Anthropic's research-preview app comes to you with what needs attention and keeps working after you put the phone down. Riley Brown's 10-hour test finds channels, a thread per task and voice editing of slide decks, and lists no model picker and no local Claude Code sessions as the gaps.

executive_summary.headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro landed with near-Opus claims and an independent test that disagrees.
executive_summary.body: Moonshot reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 66.4% for Opus 5.5, with open weights promised by Nov 4. AICodeKing's six-task build test scored it 5.37 out of 10, sixth of eleven, so run your own task before switching.

executive_summary.headline: AI is building models and running science: Flint was designed by an automated research system, and GPT-Rosalind agents read a mouse brain atlas in 32 minutes.
executive_summary.body: Recursive's 40B Flint model runs at more than 125 tokens per second on a MacBook Pro, and OpenAI with Scripps Research and PerturbAI had thousands of agents analyze millions of brain cells in 32 minutes, a job they estimate takes people months to a year.

top_picks.title: How I'm Actually Using Claude Duet (After 10 Hours of Testing)
top_picks.summary: Anthropic's Claude Duet is a standalone iOS and web agent app that organizes work into channels, gives every task its own thread and edits slide decks by voice. Riley Brown spent about 10 hours using it for business, content, apps and presentations; he lists no model picker, no local Claude Code sessions and a weaker voice mode than ChatGPT's as the gaps.
top_picks.author: Riley Brown

secondary_urls.label: Anthropic's official 'Introducing Claude Duet' video (research preview, waitlist for US Pro and Max)
Alex Finn's Duet vs Grok Bot comparison

key_takeaways: Duet is organized as channels (he kept content, finances and artifacts), with a thread for each task that shows states like working and ready for review.
Voice mode on a phone can edit a slide deck: he dictated line breaks, bullets and a new slide after slide 19.
He says Duet asks for approval before sending messages, payments, signatures and deletions, and that agent tasks run 15 to 40 minutes.
suggested_actions: Join the Duet waitlist if you are on a US Pro or Max plan, and plan a content channel and an artifacts channel before you start.
Set a daily artifact-recap routine in a channel so long-running agent work resurfaces on its own.
Run the same task in Duet and in your current agent and compare thread and approval behavior.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: A proactive agent that comes to you with what needs attention is a new operating model for a founder's day. Give one agent a channel per business function, let it draft decks and follow-ups while you are away, and review only what lands in ready-for-review.

top_picks.title: How I'd Build & Sell AI Voice Agents With NEW GPT-Live-1 (Full Course)
top_picks.summary: A 36-minute build of an AI receptionist with Codex, LiveKit and a Telnyx phone number that answers from a knowledge base, transfers live calls and books Google Calendar appointments, plus a client dashboard. It closes with niche, moat and pricing advice, and the creator recommends trades, clinics and professional services over hair salons. GPT-Live-1 costs $0.05 per minute for the voice layer in the API.
top_picks.author: Brendan Jowett

secondary_urls.label: OpenAI: GPT-Live-1 in the API ($0.05 per minute, front-end voice layer)

key_takeaways: The stack is Codex for code, LiveKit for voice infrastructure, Telnyx for a number that supports live transfer (about $1 upfront and $1 per month) and Railway for hosting bookings and the dashboard.
Test calls covered a knowledge-base answer, a transfer to a human and a 30-minute calendar booking.
His pricing advice is a fixed-price build with one or two months of monitoring, then a monthly retainer.
suggested_actions: Pick one business where a missed call costs a job (plumbing, a clinic, an accountant) and build the receptionist for its real phone line.
Add the AI-disclosure line and a transfer number for emergencies before the first live call.
Price it as build plus monitoring retainer, as the creator suggests.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: A phone line that never misses a booking is a build you can ship in a weekend. Pick one service business, give it a receptionist that books straight into its calendar, and sell the monitoring as the recurring revenue.

top_picks.title: Claude's New Live Dashboards Are Amazing
top_picks.summary: Skill Leap AI shows seven Claude live dashboards that refresh each time they are opened: Gmail emails awaiting a reply, Stripe recurring revenue, Stripe failed payments and churn by plan, QuickBooks profit, cash and runway, a Google Calendar time audit, an Ahrefs tracker of AI-search citations and a five-app morning command center. Anthropic's dashboards are in beta on paid Claude plans.
top_picks.author: Skill Leap AI
key_takeaways: Each dashboard connects one app (Gmail, Stripe, QuickBooks, Calendar or Ahrefs) and updates on open instead of on a schedule.
The Stripe examples cover recurring revenue, failed payments and churn by subscription plan.
The creator also shows how to check where any number in a dashboard came from.
suggested_actions: Start with the Stripe or QuickBooks dashboard and compare its numbers to your own books for one week.
Build the morning cockpit from the five tools you open first each day.
Use the creator's linked prompt pack as a starting point and adapt the wording to your own plan names.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Your Monday metrics meeting can be a page that is already up to date when you open it. Connect billing, books and inbox once, ask for one cockpit, and retire the weekly spreadsheet pull.

top_picks.title: The End of Seedance? Topview T1 Is 3x Cheaper (I Tested Everything)
top_picks.summary: Topview's new T1 video model costs $6.60 for 30 seconds at 1080p against $17.55 for Seedance 2.5, which Topview calls 62% less. In ten head-to-head tests Seedance clearly won prompt adherence, both fight scenes and dancing, and AI Samson's verdict is to use T1 for quiet, story-led scenes and keep Seedance for action and physics.
top_picks.author: AI Samson
key_takeaways: T1 held a character's face and scar across shots, but small on-screen text turned illegible.
Two-person dialogue came down to taste: T1 looked crisper, Seedance more cinematic.
He paid for the generations himself; HeyGen sponsors the video and Topview does not.
suggested_actions: Split your next video batch by scene type and render talking, story-led shots on T1 and action shots on Seedance.
Run your own 10-clip test with the creator's free prompt pack before moving a client over.
Track cost per finished second, not per generation.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: A 62% cut on video generation turns a one-ad budget into a three-ad test. Route dialogue and product shots to the cheaper model, keep the premium model for action, and ship more variants per campaign.

top_picks.title: AI Science Requires Physical Labs To Scale | Nenad Tomašev
top_picks.summary: Google DeepMind's Nenad Tomašev says AI agents can already generate hypotheses in biomedicine and materials science, but sciences that are not purely computational need physical labs to confirm them, because some will be false. He argues science will stay a human endeavor and calls for more experts and laboratories alongside the AI investment.
top_picks.author: Nenad Tomašev (Google DeepMind) with MTS
key_takeaways: Agentic AI can derive new hypotheses, and many are usable in practice, in his words.
The bottleneck moves downstream to validation, which needs physical laboratory infrastructure and human experts.
The last chapter covers managing agent swarms.
suggested_actions: If you work with a lab, map which hypotheses an agent could generate this month and which bench step would test each one.
Budget for validation capacity at the same time as AI tooling.
Use chapters 2:07 and 21:43 for the infrastructure and swarm-management pieces.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: The scarce resource in AI-driven discovery is the bench that tests the ideas. Pair every agent that proposes experiments with a fast, cheap way to run them, and the pipeline of tested ideas grows with it.
top_picks.why_it_matters: AI-for-science item: includes a +0.5 score bonus on a base of 7.

items.title: Flint - The First RSI Coding Model?
items.summary: Recursive's Flint is a 40B-parameter mixture-of-experts coding model with 2.5B active parameters and Apache 2.0 weights, designed by an automated research system called the Eureka Machine in under four months. Recursive reports more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, and Sam Witteveen contrasts that with about 13 tokens per second for the dense Qwen 3.8 27B on an M4.
items.author: Sam Witteveen

secondary_urls.label: ThursdAI interview with the Recursive team

key_takeaways: Recursive credits the Eureka Machine with the expert layout, the 4-bit quantization recipe and custom Metal and GPU kernels.
Witteveen shows how to run it through Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and vLLM, and demos the NVFP4 build on an RTX PRO 6000.
On ThursdAI, guest Prince Canuma ranks it among his top three local coding models and reports up to 8 parallel agents on an M5 Max.
suggested_actions: Pull the Hugging Face weights and run your own agent loop on a laptop to see whether the speed changes what you automate.
Time it against the dense local model you use today on one real coding task.
Read the Recursive post's section on how the Eureka Machine searched architectures, then try the same idea on a small model of your own.
items.enterprise_translation: A model built by an automated research loop and fast enough for dozens of agent calls on a laptop changes the economics of local agents. Put it on a team laptop, point your agent harness at it, and price your next automation at zero tokens.

items.title: Non-Technical Business Owner's Guide To Claude Code (Setup, Tools, First Build)

items.author: Russell Barnes
key_takeaways: GitHub stores the work and Vercel publishes it, which is how the first tool ends up at a link you can send.
A consistent folder structure with a CLAUDE.md makes each later project start smarter.
Dictating prompts instead of typing them is his daily shortcut.
suggested_actions: Build one internal tool for your business this week and publish it to a private link.
Copy his folder structure as your template for every new project.

The tour covers CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks and goal loops.
It also adds Chrome DevTools MCP to the setup.
suggested_actions: Add one hook that runs your tests after every edit.
Split your next feature into two worktrees and run both agents at once.

items.author: Max Explains
items.enterprise_translation: Most of the batch is going after businesses, so consumer AI is the open lane. Look at which categories the batch skips and prototype in one this month.

items.title: My AI Agent Picks: What I'd Use and Why

items.author: The AI Advantage
items.enterprise_translation: Start an always-on agent with one booking flow and one daily brief. Within a week you will see which agent fits how you work, and you will have hours of scheduling and reading handed off.
